**Mechanism: dirty-page spilling.**

During a write transaction, every page you touch is copied into malloc'd memory and tracked on the transaction's dirty list — `MDB_txn.mt_u.dirty_list`, an `MDB_ID2L` array of `MDB_ID2 {pgno, page *}` pairs — with remaining capacity accounted in `txn->mt_dirty_room`. When an update needs more pages than the dirty room allows:

- `mdb_cursor_put()` calls **`mdb_page_spill()`** before performing the write. It estimates how many pages the key/data will need; if dirty room is insufficient, it picks the least-recently-dirtied pages (entries carry a dirty-generation stamp), writes them out to the environment file early (the same write path `mdb_page_flush()` uses at commit; msync-style in `MDB_WRITEMAP` mode), frees their buffers, and removes them from the dirty list — reclaiming room so the transaction can continue instead of failing. The txn is flagged `MDB_TXN_SPILLS`.
- `mdb_page_touch()` (via `mdb_page_alloc()`, inserting with `mdb_id2l_insert()`) is the allocation/dirtying side constrained by that accounting; if a page that was already spilled gets dirtied again, `mdb_page_unspill()` puts it back on the dirty list so it's rewritten at commit.
- At commit, `mdb_txn_commit()` → `mdb_page_flush()` writes what's left, then the dirty pages are released. If spill cannot free enough room, the transaction fails with `MDB_TXN_FULL` ("transaction has too many dirty pages").

This is why LMDB can run arbitrarily large transactions despite a bounded dirty list (in newer code the list also grows up to a hard cap before spilling kicks in).

ANSWER: Dirty-page spilling — when the dirty list runs out of room (`MDB_txn.mt_dirty_room` / `mt_u.dirty_list`, an `MDB_ID2L` of `MDB_ID2` entries), `mdb_page_spill()` (called from `mdb_cursor_put`) writes the least-recently-dirtied pages to disk early and removes/frees them so the txn continues; `mdb_page_touch()`/`mdb_page_alloc()` do the dirtying, `mdb_page_unspill()` re-dirties a spilled page touched again, `mdb_page_flush()` writes the remainder at commit, and `MDB_TXN_FULL` is the failure mode when no room can be reclaimed.
